correctness.rationale: For invariant f and any dual x, replicate the G-orbit as normalized test rows |G|^(-1/p)gx. Transitivity within each orbit yields coordinate p-costs c_a(x)=|O_a|^(-1)sum_{i in O_a}|x_i|^p. Normalizing by C=max_a c_a gives |f(x)|^p<=||f||^p C. For any k unit positive invariant functions, their pointwise supremum has p-norm budget ≤sum_a sum_s c_a(x_s)≤r and independently ≤k by p-convexity, giving Γ_k≤min(k,r)^(1/p). Positive orbit averages h_a(x)=avg_{i in O_a}|x_i| have norm exactly one, tested on indicator rows with disjoint orbit supports; their supremum attains min(k,r)^(1/p). For p=∞ free AM norm gives Γ=1. For p finite Γ_2=1 iff r=1, including n=1 and trivial orbit configurations. Independently checked rational binary orbit-cost inequalities for partition (1,2,2), p=1,2,3 and exact indicator-row witnesses; non-integer p follows analytic norm argument, not these checks.
